listings.title: Learning Planet Youth Design Challenge
listings.summary:
The Learning Planet Youth Design Challenge (LPYDC) is a launchpad for youth-led social impact projects.

The participants, aged between 15 and 26, pitch projects online that can create real-world impact in their communities.

Projects should align with one of the following themes:

Peace & Democracy
Mental Health & Wellbeing
Environment & Climate
listings.who:
1) Young people aged 15-26 years
2) Applicants from anywhere in the world
3) Individuals or teams with projects addressing social and environmental challenges
listings.dates: Applications open 14 Oct 2026. Apply by 7 Jan 2027, 11:59 PM Nepal time.
listings.benefits:
Training
- 60 shortlisted projects will benefit from online training, including targeted mentorship, masterclasses and practical tools to develop their project.

Prizes
- 12 will be selected by the jury as ambassadors and will receive a $1,000 grant to advance their projects.

Recognition
- Certification by the United Nations University Hub for Future of Learning with Youth (UNU FLY) .

** The 12 ambassadors will be invited to international events and receive tailored networking to advance their projects. **
steps: Register from given official link

listings.title: Call for Female Nepali Artists
listings.summary: The Australian Embassy in Kathmandu is inviting Expressions of Interest (EOI) from female Nepali artists and women-led creative groups to design and paint two new murals on the Embassy's front walls.
listings.who:
1) Female individual artists
2) Women-led artist collectives
3) Women-led creative organisations and cultural institutions
4) Female practitioners with experience in mural art, public art, traditional art, community arts, or related creative fields
listings.dates: Applications open 23 Oct 2026. Apply by 7 Nov 2026, 11:59 PM Nepal time.
listings.benefits: US$2,000 contribution towards artist fees and creative labour
steps: Register Now

listings.title: Call For Volunteers
listings.summary:
Volunteer at WordCamp Nepal 2027
Ready to be part of Nepal’s biggest WordPress event?

WordCamp Nepal 2027 takes place on January 29 and 30, 2027, in Nepalgunj. We’re looking for energetic, motivated, and dependable volunteers to help make this event another memorable one.

Volunteering at WordCamp is about more than helping behind the scenes. It’s about creating an experience that inspires thousands of people in Nepal’s growing WordPress community. Whether you’re a WordPress veteran, designer, developer, content creator, or simply a volunteer at heart, this is your chance to participate, network, and learn.

Deadline for form submission is October 31, 2026
listings.who: Anyone passionate about WordPress, whether experienced or brand new, is welcome to join.
listings.dates: 20 to 31 Oct 2026. Applications open 20 Oct 2026. Apply by 7 Nov 2026, 11:59 PM Nepal time.
listings.benefits:
Be part of something bigger: Join a lively, open celebration of WordPress, open source, and digital innovation.
Grow your network: Meet global contributors, community leaders, developers, business owners, and fellow WordPress fans.
Gain real-world experience: From event planning to media support, volunteering builds your teamwork, leadership, and organizational skills.
Enjoy special perks: Free admission, event swag, an exclusive volunteer T-shirt, access to the pre-party and after-party, and memories that last a lifetime.
steps: Register
Team
Submit

listings.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
listings.summary: A two-day global hackathon where teams use open space and Earth data to solve challenges set by NASA and its partner agencies. Hundreds of local events run worldwide, and there is a virtual option for anyone without a local event.
listings.who: Open to anyone. Teams can have up to 6 people. Check the official rules for any age limits.
listings.dates: 14 to 15 Nov 2026. Project submissions open 14 Nov at 9:00 and close 15 Nov at 23:59, local time.
listings.cost: No fee listed on the official page
listings.benefits: Global judging and awards, and real experience with NASA open data
steps: Register on the official 2026 Space Apps site.
Choose an in-person or virtual local event, or the virtual Universal Event.
Form a team of up to 6 people.
Pick a challenge and submit your project before 23:59 local time on 15 Nov.
listings.notes: When we checked, the official page did not list a local event in Nepal. You can still take part through the virtual Universal Event.

listings.title: Hacktoberfest 2026
listings.summary: A month-long open-source celebration. In 2026 it focuses on in-person and online events about building and learning with open-source AI and open-weight models, instead of counting pull requests.
listings.who: Anyone aged 13 or older, subject to country eligibility. Under-18s should ask the event host about parental permission.
listings.dates: Runs throughout October 2026. The participant dashboard opened by 1 Oct.
listings.cost: Almost all Fests are free; some pop-ups happen at ticketed conferences
listings.benefits: Sticker pack for completing the listed activities, DEV badge, learning sessions
steps: Sign in to My Hacktoberfest with a MyMLH account.
Optionally connect your DEV account for the DEV badge.
Join an online event (DEV Challenges, MLH livestreams, Global Hack Week) or register for an in-person Fest.
Complete the activities listed on your participant page.
listings.notes: Pull and merge requests no longer count toward Hacktoberfest rewards in 2026. The FAQ says the event runs throughout October but does not give an exact end time.

listings.title: PgConf.Nepal 2026
listings.organizer: Nepal PostgreSQL User Group, with Kathmandu University and IOE Pulchowk Campus
listings.summary: Nepal's PostgreSQL conference: talks and knowledge sharing about the PostgreSQL database, with pre-conference training. A strong event for students interested in databases and backend development.
listings.who: Developers, database professionals and students interested in PostgreSQL.
listings.dates: 18 to 21 Nov 2026 (the official site shows both 18 to 21 Nov and 20 to 21 Nov, so confirm the training and conference days on the schedule).
listings.cost: See the Pricing page on the official site
listings.benefits: Talks, pre-conference training, networking with the database community
steps: Open the official site and check the Schedule and Venue pages.
Check the Pricing page for ticket types.
Register through the site's Register link.
Contact info@pgconf.org.np for questions about student access.
listings.notes: The official home page lists two different date ranges. We will update this listing once the schedule confirms the split between training and conference days.

listings.title: AI Conf 2027, Kathmandu
listings.summary: Three days of talks and keynotes on building, shipping and scaling AI, from research to production, plus a community hike around the Kathmandu valley. The call for speakers is open.
listings.who: Engineers, designers, founders, researchers and students working with AI. Speaker proposals are open to people who use or build AI in products and workflows.
listings.benefits: About 500 attendees from across Asia; accommodation for accepted speakers
steps: Sign up for updates on the official site to hear when tickets open.
To speak, submit a talk of about 20 minutes through the call-for-speakers form on the site.
Proposals are reviewed on a rolling basis, so submit early.
listings.notes: The official site does not yet name the venue or ticket prices.

listings.title: Hult Prize 2026-27
listings.summary: A global startup competition for university students. Teams build a venture that addresses one of the UN Sustainable Development Goals and compete from campus rounds upward.
listings.who: Teams of 2 to 4. Every member must be enrolled in a degree-seeking programme and be at least 18 by 28 Feb 2027.
listings.dates: 2026-27 competition cycle. Register your team's interest on the official site.
listings.cost: Not stated on the registration page
listings.benefits: Startup experience, mentorship and a global stage; see the site for prize details
steps: Form a team of 2 to 4 enrolled students.
Choose the Sustainable Development Goal your startup will address.
Complete the three-step registration form on the official site.
Ask your college whether it runs an on-campus round.
listings.notes: The registration page does not list competition deadlines yet.

listings.title: Microsoft Imagine Cup 2027
listings.summary: Microsoft's student startup competition for student founders building a product. Registering unlocks Azure credits to build and test a minimum viable product.
listings.who: Student teams of up to 4. Every team member must register on the Imagine Cup site. Check the FAQ for age and country rules.
listings.dates: Deadlines are announced on Imagine Cup's official channels.
listings.cost: Not stated on the official page
listings.benefits: Up to USD 5,000 in Azure credits after registration
steps: Read the 2027 competition page and FAQ.
Form a team of up to 4 students.
Each member registers on the Imagine Cup site.
Use the Azure credits to build your MVP and follow official channels for deadlines.
listings.notes: The official page does not list prizes or deadlines yet.

listings.title: picoCTF 2027
listings.summary: A beginner-friendly online cybersecurity capture-the-flag competition. The practice gym stays open all year, so you can train before the next competition.
listings.who: Players aged 13 or older; under-18s need consent from a parent or guardian. Teams of up to 5. Prize eligibility depends on region and school level.
listings.dates: The 2027 dates are not announced yet. The 2026 competition ran 9 to 19 March 2026, with registration from 1 Feb.
listings.benefits: Hands-on cybersecurity practice, a scoreboard and prizes for eligible categories
steps: Create a free picoCTF account.
Practise in the picoGym until the 2027 competition opens.
Form a team of up to 5 and register when registration opens.
listings.notes: Based on the 2026 timing, expect registration around February and the competition in March. We will update this listing when dates are announced.

listings.title: Kaggle Competitions
listings.summary: Data science and machine learning competitions that run all year, including beginner "Getting Started" competitions with tutorials and public notebooks to learn from.
listings.who: Anyone with a free Kaggle account. Each competition has its own rules.
listings.dates: Always running. Each competition has its own deadline.
listings.benefits: Real datasets, rankings for your profile, prizes on some competitions
steps: Create a free Kaggle account.
Start with a Getting Started competition.
Read the public notebooks, then submit your own model.
listings.notes: This is a general listing for the platform. Check each competition's rules, deadline and prize eligibility.

listings.title: Google Summer of Code 2027
listings.summary: A remote programme where contributors new to open source write code for open-source organisations with a mentor, and receive a stipend.
listings.who: People new to open-source contribution. Check the official rules for age and eligibility details.
listings.dates: The 2027 timeline is not announced yet. In 2026, contributor applications ran 16 to 31 March, with coding from 25 May.
listings.benefits: Paid stipend, mentorship and real open-source experience
steps: Learn Git and make small contributions to open-source projects now.
When organisations are announced (February in 2026), shortlist two or three.
Talk to their mentors and read their project ideas.
Submit a proposal during the contributor application period.
listings.notes: The best time to prepare is now: organisations look for applicants who already contributed to their project.

listings.title: Outreachy internships, May 2027 cohort
listings.summary: Paid, remote three-month internships in open source and open science, for people who face under-representation or systemic bias in the tech industry where they live.
listings.who: See the Outreachy eligibility rules; eligibility is checked in the initial application.
listings.dates: Initial applications for the December 2026 cohort closed on 31 Aug 2026. For the May 2026 cohort, initial applications opened in early February, so expect the May 2027 round early in 2027.
listings.benefits: Paid internship stipend and mentorship
steps: Read the eligibility rules on the Outreachy site.
Submit the initial application when the May 2027 round opens.
If accepted to the contribution period, contribute to a project and record your contributions.
Submit a final application for the project you contributed to.
listings.notes: The December 2026 cohort's internship runs 7 Dec 2026 to 8 Mar 2027.

listings.title: LFX Mentorship, Spring 2027 term
listings.summary: Paid mentorships on Linux Foundation open-source projects. Full-time mentorships last 12 weeks and part-time ones 24 weeks.
listings.who: Students and early-career developers; each project lists its own skills and requirements.
listings.dates: The Spring term runs 1 Mar to 31 May. Projects are listed in mid-January and mentee applications stay open for about 4 weeks.
listings.benefits: Stipend paid in two halves, at the midterm and at the end
steps: Create an LFX account and complete your profile.
Watch for Spring projects in mid-January.
Apply to up to the number of projects allowed, with a short cover letter and any tasks the mentor sets.
listings.notes: There are also Summer (Jun to Aug) and Fall (Sep to Nov) terms. Dates can vary by project.

listings.title: MLH Fellowship
listings.summary: A 12-week remote programme where fellows learn software engineering by working on real projects with peers and mentors, with an educational stipend.
listings.who: Aspiring software engineers and technologists. See the official FAQ for detailed eligibility.
listings.dates: Applications are accepted for upcoming batches.
listings.benefits: Educational stipend; tracks in Software Engineering, Production Engineering (SRE) and Web3 Engineering
steps: Choose a track.
Prepare a code sample you wrote yourself.
Apply on the official site and check the FAQ for batch dates.
listings.notes: The official page does not list the next batch dates.

listings.title: Chevening Scholarships 2027-28
listings.summary: The UK government's fully funded scholarship for a one-year master's degree in the UK, for future leaders with a clear plan to make a positive impact.
listings.who: Applicants from Chevening-eligible countries. Check chevening.org for the full eligibility criteria.
listings.dates: Applications for 2027-28 closed on 6 Oct 2026. Results are expected in June 2027, with study starting in September or October 2027.
listings.benefits: Tuition fees, living expenses and return flights to the UK
steps: Check eligibility on chevening.org.
Prepare three UK master's course choices.
Draft your leadership, networking and career plan essays early.
Apply when the next round opens.
listings.notes: Missed this round? Start preparing your essays and course choices now for the next one.

listings.title: MEXT (Japanese Government) Scholarship 2027
listings.organizer: Government of Japan, via the Embassy of Japan in Nepal
listings.summary: Japanese government scholarships for Nepali students, in four categories: research (postgraduate), undergraduate, specialized training college and teacher training.
listings.who: Nepali students; each category has its own age and education rules on the embassy page.
listings.dates: Applications for all 2027 categories are closed. The research category's screening results are posted on the embassy page.
listings.benefits: Government scholarship for study in Japan
steps: Read the category pages on the Embassy of Japan in Nepal website.
Prepare documents and academic records ahead of the next round.
Apply only through the embassy's official process.
listings.notes: The embassy warns that anyone who charges a fee for these procedures has no relation to the MEXT Scholarship.

listings.title: Fulbright Master's Program (Nepal)
listings.summary: The U.S. government's Fulbright programme for graduate study in the United States, run in Nepal by the Fulbright Commission.
listings.who: Nepali graduates; criteria are published with each competition.
listings.dates: Each competition's dates are announced on the Commission's website.
listings.benefits: Funded graduate study in the U.S.
steps: Check the Commission's website for the next competition.
Prepare transcripts, test scores and essays early.
Apply through the Commission only.
listings.notes: We have not yet verified the next competition's dates. Always confirm on the Commission's website.

listings.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters
listings.summary: Joint master's programmes run by groups of European universities, with EU-funded scholarships for top applicants. Students study in at least two countries.
listings.who: Bachelor's graduates worldwide; each programme sets its own entry requirements.
listings.dates: Deadlines vary by programme. Check each programme's own website.
listings.benefits: Scholarships covering study costs for selected students
steps: Search the catalogue for programmes in your field.
Open each programme's site for its deadline and requirements.
Apply directly to the programme.
listings.notes: This is a general listing for the catalogue. Each programme publishes its own dates.

listings.title: DAAD Scholarships for Germany
listings.summary: A searchable database of scholarships for studying and researching in Germany, filtered by your country, subject and level.
listings.who: International students and graduates; each scholarship has its own criteria.
listings.benefits: Funding for study or research in Germany
steps: Open the database and select Nepal as your country of origin.
Filter by subject and status (student, graduate, PhD).
Read each scholarship's requirements and deadline.
listings.notes: This is a general listing for the database.

listings.title: GitHub Student Developer Pack
listings.summary: A bundle of developer tools, cloud credits and learning platforms that are free or discounted for students, including GitHub Pro.
listings.who: Students who verify their student status with GitHub. Some partner offers have their own age limits.
listings.dates: Always open while you are a student.
listings.benefits: GitHub Pro, a free JetBrains subscription, Azure credit, GitHub Copilot Student for verified students, and more
steps: Create a GitHub account with your college email if you have one.
Apply for student benefits from your GitHub education settings.
Upload proof of enrolment if asked.
Activate the partner offers you need.
listings.notes: Many offers are time-limited trials or credits, so activate them when you are ready to use them.

listings.title: Google Developer Groups on Campus
listings.summary: University developer clubs that run workshops, study jams and projects. Join your college's chapter, or apply to lead one.
listings.who: University students; leads are selected through Google's application process.
listings.dates: Chapters run events through the year.
listings.benefits: Workshops, a peer community, and leadership experience
steps: Search the community site for a chapter at your college.
Join to get event invitations.
If there is no chapter, look for the lead application on Google's developer site.
listings.notes: This is a general listing for the programme.

listings.title: freeCodeCamp Certifications
listings.summary: Free, self-paced curricula with projects and certifications in web development, JavaScript, Python, data analysis and more.
listings.who: Anyone. No experience needed.
listings.benefits: Project-based certifications you can add to your CV
steps: Create a free account.
Start with the web design curriculum if you are new.
Build every project yourself and push it to GitHub.
listings.notes: Certifications mean most when your projects are your own work and visible on GitHub.

listings.title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy
listings.summary: Free online training in web application security, with interactive labs on vulnerabilities such as SQL injection, XSS and access control.
listings.who: Anyone interested in web security; basic web knowledge helps.
listings.benefits: Hands-on labs and learning paths
steps: Create a free account.
Follow a learning path from the start.
Solve the labs and write short notes on each one.
listings.notes: Practise only on the labs and systems you have permission to test.

listings.title: BSides Kathmandu 2026
listings.summary: Nepal's first BSides security conference: a one-day, community-driven event with technical talks, hands-on villages, a live capture-the-flag competition and a stage for first-time speakers.
listings.who: Security professionals, students and anyone curious about cybersecurity.
listings.cost: Ticket details available from the organizers by email
listings.benefits: Talks, hands-on villages, a live CTF and a first-time speaker stage
steps: Follow updates on bsidesktm.com and @bsidesktm on X.
Email info@bsidesktm.com for ticket and registration details.
Practise for the live CTF on picoGym, OverTheWire or TryHackMe.
If you want to give your first talk, ask the organizers about the first-time speaker stage.
listings.notes: The official site does not yet list ticket prices, a call for papers or CTF rules. We will update this listing as they are announced.

listings.title: WordCamp Nepal 2027
listings.summary: Nepal's national WordPress conference for developers, designers, writers and businesses that build with WordPress. Recent WordCamps in Nepal have included a contributor day and a main conference day.
listings.who: Anyone interested in WordPress and the web, from students to professionals.
listings.dates: 29 to 30 Jan 2027, according to the dev.events listing. Confirm on the official site.
listings.cost: See the tickets page on the official site
listings.benefits: Talks, workshops, contributing to WordPress and meeting the community
steps: Open the official WordCamp Nepal 2027 site.
Check the tickets page and register early.
Look for calls for speakers, volunteers and sponsors on the site.
Plan your travel to Nepalgunj.
listings.notes: Our checker could not read the official site, so the dates come from the dev.events listing. Confirm them on nepal.wordcamp.org before booking travel.

listings.title: IEEEXtreme 20.0
listings.summary: A 24-hour global programming competition for teams of IEEE student members, usually organised through IEEE Student Branches at colleges.
listings.who: Teams of IEEE Student members, advised and proctored by an IEEE member.
listings.location: Online (often hosted at your college's IEEE Student Branch)
listings.cost: Not stated on the official page
listings.benefits: Global rankings and prizes, and a strong item for a programmer's CV
steps: Check whether your college has an IEEE Student Branch.
Become an IEEE student member if you are not one.
Form a team and find an IEEE member to act as proctor.
Register on the official site before the contest.
listings.notes: The official home page does not show the registration deadline or team size. Ask your IEEE Student Branch counsellor.

listings.title: TryHackMe Advent of Cyber 2026
listings.summary: TryHackMe's free December event with one beginner-friendly security challenge released each day. The 2025 edition had 24 challenges and a prize pool of USD 150,000.
listings.who: Anyone, from complete beginners to aspiring professionals.
listings.dates: Runs every December. The 2025 edition started on 1 Dec 2025. The 2026 dates are not announced yet.
listings.benefits: Daily guided challenges and prizes
steps: Create a free TryHackMe account.
Work through the Advent of Cyber prep track before December.
Join on day one and complete one challenge a day.
listings.notes: Prepare early with TryHackMe's Advent of Cyber prep track room.

listings.title: SANS Holiday Hack Challenge 2026
listings.summary: A free, story-driven cybersecurity game with challenges ranging from short beginner warm-ups to expert-level capstones.
listings.who: Anyone interested in cybersecurity.
listings.dates: Runs each winter. The 2025 edition opened on 5 Nov 2025 and stayed playable for about two months. The 2026 dates are not announced yet.
listings.benefits: Hands-on challenges, hints and a prize contest
steps: Create a free account when the 2026 game opens.
Start with the warm-up challenges and use the hints.
Write up what you solve; it makes a strong portfolio piece.
listings.notes: Past challenges stay online, so you can practise on earlier editions now.

listings.title: Upcoming CTFs on CTFtime
listings.summary: The global calendar of capture-the-flag competitions, with online CTFs almost every weekend and team rankings.
listings.who: Anyone; each CTF sets its own rules.
listings.benefits: Practice under pressure and a public team ranking
steps: Form a team with classmates and register it on CTFtime.
Pick CTFs marked for beginners or with a low weight first.
Write up every challenge you solve and share it.
listings.notes: This is a general listing for the calendar. Check each CTF's rules and format.

listings.title: OverTheWire Wargames
listings.summary: Free security wargames you play over SSH. Bandit teaches the Linux command line from zero and is the classic first step before real CTFs.
listings.who: Anyone; start with Bandit if you are new.
listings.benefits: Linux, networking and security skills through levels
steps: Open the Bandit wargame page.
Connect with SSH and solve level 0.
Keep notes for each level; avoid copying solutions.
listings.notes: Ideal practice before BSides Kathmandu's live CTF or picoCTF.

listings.title: Advent of Code
listings.summary: A December programming puzzle event you can solve in any language. The 2025 edition had 12 days of puzzles.
listings.who: Anyone who can program.
listings.dates: Every December. The 2026 format and dates are not announced yet.
listings.cost: Not stated on the official page
listings.benefits: Daily puzzles, private leaderboards for your class or club
steps: Pick a language you want to practise.
Create a private leaderboard for your college club.
Solve each puzzle and compare approaches afterwards.
listings.notes: Past years' puzzles stay online, so you can start practising now.

listings.title: Codeforces Contests
listings.summary: Regular online competitive programming rounds with global ratings, from beginner Div. 4 rounds to advanced Div. 1.
listings.who: Anyone with a free account.
listings.benefits: A public rating that recruiters and contest teams recognise
steps: Create a free account.
Start with Div. 4 or Div. 3 rounds.
Upsolve: after each contest, solve the problems you missed.
listings.notes: Steady practice here also prepares you for ICPC and interview rounds.

listings.title: Fusemachines AI Fellowship (Nepal)
listings.summary: A six-month AI and data science programme in Nepal, now in its ninth year, covering machine learning, deep learning, NLP, computer vision, generative AI and MLOps. Selected candidates receive full scholarships.
listings.who: IT students, professionals and enthusiasts with a background in programming, mathematics, computer science or software development.
listings.dates: Applications for the 2026 cohort opened in February 2026. Based on recent years, expect the next round early in 2027.
listings.benefits: Six-month AI Microdegree with live lectures, self-paced study and onsite exercises
steps: Strengthen Python, linear algebra and statistics now.
Watch the official page for the next application window.
Complete the multi-stage selection process.
listings.notes: Selection is competitive; finished ML projects on GitHub help.

listings.title: Teach For Nepal Fellowship
listings.summary: A two-year, full-time paid fellowship where graduates and young professionals teach in public schools to improve students' learning and opportunities.
listings.who: Outstanding university graduates and young professionals.
listings.dates: Check the apply page for the next cohort.
listings.benefits: Full-time paid role, training and leadership experience
steps: Read about the fellowship on the official site.
Prepare to commit two years full-time.
Apply through the official apply page.
listings.notes: The official page does not list the next deadline or stipend amount.

listings.title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS)
listings.organizer: Government of Korea (NIIED), via the Embassy of Korea in Nepal
listings.summary: Fully funded study in Korea for bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees, including a year of Korean language training, tuition, airfare and a monthly allowance.
listings.who: Nepali citizens. Undergraduate applicants must be under 25 and graduate applicants under 40, with minimum GPA or class-rank requirements.
listings.dates: In Nepal, undergraduate (GKS-U) applications for 2026 were due 6 to 10 Oct 2025, and graduate (GKS-G) applications ran 12 to 25 Feb 2026. The global GKS-U 2027 embassy track opened in mid-September 2026; check the embassy's notices for Nepal's dates.
listings.when: Undergraduate around October, graduate around February
listings.benefits: Tuition, airfare, Korean language course and a monthly allowance
steps: Watch the Embassy of Korea in Nepal notice board.
Get documents attested by Nepal's Ministry of Foreign Affairs early.
Apply through Study in Korea and submit documents as the notice explains.
Shortlisted candidates are interviewed.
listings.notes: Places for Nepal are very limited (two undergraduate places in the 2026 round), so prepare strong documents early.

listings.title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
listings.summary: Harvard's famous introduction to computer science, free online: C, Python, SQL, web development and problem solving, with a final project.
listings.who: Anyone, including complete beginners.
listings.benefits: Problem sets, a final project and a certificate from CS50
steps: Watch week 0 and set up the online environment.
Do every problem set yourself.
Build a final project you can show on GitHub.
listings.notes: Study with friends, but submit your own work; the course is strict about academic honesty.

listings.title: Elements of AI
listings.summary: A free online introduction to artificial intelligence for non-experts, explaining what AI is, what it can and cannot do, and how it is built.
listings.who: Anyone; no programming or maths needed for the introduction.
listings.benefits: A clear foundation in AI concepts and a certificate on completion
steps: Create a free account.
Complete the chapters and exercises.
Follow up with Kaggle Learn to start building models.
listings.notes: A good first step before the Fusemachines AI Fellowship or Kaggle competitions.

listings.title: Cisco Networking Academy
listings.summary: Free self-paced courses in networking, cybersecurity, Python and more, including introductions to cybersecurity and networking basics.
listings.who: Anyone; some advanced courses run through partner institutions.
listings.benefits: Structured courses, labs and digital badges
steps: Create a free NetAcad account.
Start with an introduction to cybersecurity or networking basics.
Add earned badges to your LinkedIn profile.
listings.notes: Check each course page; some instructor-led courses require enrolling through an academy.

listings.title: Kaggle Learn
listings.summary: Short, free, hands-on courses in Python, pandas, machine learning, SQL and data visualisation, run in the browser.
listings.who: Anyone with a free Kaggle account.
listings.benefits: Hands-on notebooks and certificates of completion
steps: Start with Python, then Pandas and Intro to Machine Learning.
Join a Getting Started competition.
Publish one notebook with your own analysis.
listings.notes: Pairs well with Kaggle competitions on the Hackathons board.

listings.title: Google Machine Learning Crash Course
listings.summary: Google's free, practical introduction to machine learning, with videos, interactive visualisations and coding exercises.
listings.who: Anyone with basic Python and algebra.
listings.benefits: A solid ML foundation from Google engineers
steps: Review basic Python and algebra.
Work through the modules in order.
Apply what you learn on a small dataset of your own.

listings.title: UN Online Volunteering
listings.summary: Remote volunteer assignments for UN agencies and partner organisations working on sustainable development, from design and data to translation and research.
listings.who: Anyone aged 18 or older.
listings.dates: New assignments are posted all year.
listings.benefits: Real project experience and an electronic certificate of appreciation
steps: Sign up on the Unified Volunteering Platform.
Filter for online assignments that match your skills.
Apply with a short, specific message about what you can do.
listings.notes: Assignments are limited to 20 hours a week for up to 12 weeks.

listings.title: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Mapping
listings.summary: Map buildings and roads from satellite imagery to support disaster response and development projects. You can map from your laptop in any spare hour.
listings.who: Anyone with an OpenStreetMap account.
listings.benefits: Mapping and GIS skills, and visible impact

listings.benefits: Writing, research and open-knowledge experience
steps: Create a Wikipedia account.
Start by improving short articles.
Cite reliable sources for every fact.

listings.title: Be My Eyes
listings.summary: Help blind and low-vision people with everyday tasks through short video calls from your phone.
listings.who: Anyone aged 17 or older with a smartphone; check the app's rules.
listings.benefits: Help people directly, a few minutes at a time
steps: Install the app.
Sign up as a volunteer and choose your languages.
Answer calls when you can.

listings.title: Nepal Red Cross Society youth volunteering
listings.summary: Volunteer with Nepal Red Cross in first aid, disaster preparedness and community service across the country.
listings.who: Youth and students in Nepal; check with your district chapter.
listings.benefits: First aid training and community service experience
steps: Contact your district chapter.
Join youth or junior circles at your college.
Take part in trainings and campaigns.

listings.title: Code for Nepal
listings.summary: A nonprofit working on open data and digital literacy in Nepal, with ways for volunteers to contribute.
listings.who: Anyone interested in data and technology for Nepal.
listings.benefits: Data and civic tech experience
steps: Read about current projects.
Get in touch through the official site.
listings.notes: General listing.

listings.title: Figma for Education
listings.summary: Free Figma plans for students and educators, for design and prototyping.
listings.who: Verified students and educators.
listings.benefits: Professional design tools
steps: Apply with your student details.
Use it for project and portfolio designs.

listings.title: Microsoft 365 Education
listings.summary: Office apps such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint free for eligible students with a school email.
listings.who: Students at eligible institutions.
listings.benefits: Office apps and OneDrive storage
steps: Enter your school email on the official page.
Follow the sign-up steps.

listings.title: Autodesk Education
listings.summary: Free educational access to Autodesk software such as AutoCAD, Fusion and Maya for students.
listings.who: Students and educators at eligible institutions.
listings.benefits: Professional design and engineering software
steps: Create an education account.
Verify your eligibility.
Download the software you need.

listings.title: Unity Student Plan
listings.summary: Free access to Unity Pro features and learning resources for students learning game development.
listings.who: Students aged 16 or older; check current eligibility.
listings.benefits: Professional game engine features
steps: Verify your student status.
Install Unity Hub.
Follow Unity Learn pathways.

listings.title: NISC: Nepalgunj IT Students Community
listings.summary: A student IT community in Nepalgunj and a SWABUD community partner, bringing students in western Nepal together to learn, build and share opportunities.
listings.who: IT students in and around Nepalgunj.
listings.benefits: Peers, events and local opportunities shared through SWABUD
steps: Read about the partnership on SWABUD.
Contact SWABUD to be introduced to NISC.

listings.title: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS) 2026
listings.organizer: NAAMII (NepAl Applied Mathematics and Informatics Institute for research)
listings.summary: The seventh Annual Nepal AI School: about ten days of AI lectures and hands-on labs taught by international researchers, held in person near Kathmandu.
listings.who: Students (full-time, or graduated in the last six months), start-up, academic and other professionals with a CS, engineering, maths, AI or data background or interest.
listings.dates: Student scholarship deadline for applicants in Nepal: 31 Oct 2026. General (non-scholarship) applications close 15 Nov 2026. The school runs 28 Dec 2026 to 7 Jan 2027.
listings.cost: Registration fee; full and partial scholarships available (two full scholarships per province cover registration, stay, travel and meals)
listings.benefits: Lectures and labs from international AI researchers, lunch and refreshments, a hike, and a network of Nepali and international AI learners
steps: Read the application page and pick your category (student, start-up, academic or other professional).
Prepare your CV and, if a student, proof of enrolment as separate PDFs; answer the application questions in 250 words or fewer each.
Submit the Google Form linked on the page before 31 Oct 2026 for a scholarship, or 15 Nov 2026 otherwise.
listings.notes: One of the best AI learning opportunities held inside Nepal. If you need funding, apply by 31 Oct for the scholarship round. Write your own answers: mostly AI-written responses are disqualified.

listings.title: LOCUS National Technological Festival
listings.summary: Nepal's national-level technology festival run by Pulchowk engineering students, with project exhibitions, hackathons, coding contests and robotics competitions.
listings.who: Engineering and IT students across Nepal; some pre-events are for +2 students.
listings.dates: LOCUS 2027 is the 23rd edition; dates are not announced yet. The main exhibition is usually held early in the year (2023 ran 27 to 29 Jan).
listings.cost: Exhibition visits are usually free; some competitions charge entry
listings.benefits: Show your project nationally, compete in hackathons and coding contests, meet companies and engineering students
steps: Follow LOCUS on its official site and social pages for the 2027 pre-event list.
Pick a pre-event (hackathon, coding contest, robotics) and register before it closes.
Register your project for the exhibition if you have one to show.
listings.notes: Pre-events such as hackathons often run in the months before the main exhibition, so start watching from November.

listings.title: TechSprint Hackathon (Nepal Engineering College)
listings.summary: A collegiate hackathon at Nepal Engineering College with team challenges, a penetration testing challenge and a symposium.
listings.who: Undergraduate students currently enrolled in any college or university, in teams of 2 to 4.
listings.dates: The 2026 edition was held on 17 Jan 2026 (pen-testing challenge 17 to 19 Jan). The next edition has not been announced.
listings.cost: Not stated on the official page
listings.benefits: NPR 120K+ in prizes in 2026, cash prizes and swag
steps: Form a team of 2 to 4 undergraduate students.
Watch the official page for the next registration window.
Register your team before seats fill.
listings.notes: Also a good place for security students: the 2026 edition included an NCHL penetration testing challenge.

listings.title: KMC HackVerse (BCA hackathon)
listings.summary: A 48-hour national hackathon for BCA students, where shortlisted teams build their proposed projects.
listings.who: Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA) students from colleges across Nepal.
listings.dates: The 2026 edition ran 19 to 21 Jun 2026; 15 teams were selected from 50+ proposals. The next edition has not been announced.
listings.benefits: NPR 1,00,000 in prize money in 2026, plus partner vouchers
steps: Form a BCA team and draft a clear project proposal.
Watch for the next call for proposals.
If shortlisted, prepare your stack and plan before the 48 hours start.
listings.notes: Proposal-based selection: a sharp problem statement matters more than a long feature list.
